comments.value:
This is an absolutely awful idea on multiple points so let's go over them.
1. DMCA as a system is incredibly broken and ripe for abuse, especially as a "Guilty before proven innocent" system like you're requesting. It would be weaponized within microseconds of implementation for people wanting to spark drama.
2. There's enough cross-contamination in terms of people kitbashing models together to sell (whether with or without permission from the original creator) that actually trying to enforce DMCAs in a legal capacity would be an absolute nightmare.
3. Outside of the demographic that refuse to pay for anything ever, Piracy is more often than not a service problem and not a theft issue. If people are pirating your work to such a degree that you want a DMCA system implemented, it either means the work you're selling is either not readily available in a format people can easily purchase or your work isn't quite up to snuff for the price point you're selling it at.
Overall this idea would be detrimental at best and a cataclysmic, community shattering event at worst due to how many problems this would cause in comparison to the problems you think it would solve.

This is terrible in practice if implemented in this fashion. There are several already existing routes you can go regarding DMCA and yes they do take time.  This thread has several very clear explanations of the obvious challenges this proposal makes and yes the unfortunate window of acceptance to certain things that require patience. If these are not terms you're willing to work with my recommendation is to remove your product from sale until you feel more comfortable with the solution provider.

@{62bb3c3a70a5022221383cec|full_name}: I can totally comprehend the problems with DMCA and I agree with the legal standpoint of it (aka the line considering what can be DMCA and the difficulty / time it would take to establish it)! 
Especially for avatars that are based on characters from genuine franchises! (Such as pokemon, mario, sonic, etc.) But I feel like we need to take actions regardless, because rippers/ leakers are constantly growing and being left unpunished.
Furthermore, we don't have protections for original characters that we create and the data for them are being tossed around in public domain! I can see the issues and difficulties implementing the system but I feel like it's a step to help creators and to protect private work! 
I understand what you are saying is in good intentions, but I also feel like we need some kind of change or experimentation. Or nothing will happen and our personal creations will continue to be taken advantage of.

@{62bb3c3a70a5022221383cec|full_name}: Would have made my own post pointing out how absolutely HORRID such a DMCA system would be, but this post pretty succinctly puts down most of everything I would have said.
Piracy sucks being on the receiving end, I've had my stuff ripped and reuploaded and I'm not happy that it happened. But it was also of a IP character that someone easily would make the argument "I don't own the character, so I shouldn't have uploaded it" (even though it's for all intents and purposes a form of otherwise original fan art, and it was a public avatar for anyone to use so it's not like I was making money off of it).
AND to the fact this avatar was derived from a mod I did for another game, which someone unobservant or "Trying to be a good samaritan without researching WHO uploaded the avatar" might go "Oh, someone ripped this mod for this other game and modified it to put into VRChat, I should be helpful and report this to VRChat". Which in THAT scenario, we're proposing this avatar, which many, many people use and enjoy, should be taken down immediately with zero recourse for me to do anything about it, wait the months or even year+ this would take to investigate (Which no, you would NEVER see a immediate investigation, because VRChat couldn't reasonably hire the MILLIONS of employees it would take to shift through all of the false claims that would happen IMMEDIATELY and perpetually if such a system were to be implemented), with the final outcome up completely in the air as the one employee who would EVENTUALLY get to this fraudulent claim might be as unobservant as the person who originally filed it.
Again, piracy can suck depending on the side of the fence we're on and the circumstances around it. But, assuming based on the rest of the comments this was sparked because you (the OP of this canny, not who I'm responding to) make ans sell VRChat assets, frankly need to realize a truism of the way digital sales work:
Piracy is going to happen. No matter how much people like you would try to ruin the core experience for everyone else to prevent it from happening (If it was a solved problem, no one would have a problem with Denuvo.), it will still happen. Frankly, obsessing over stopping the pirates is a fight in futility with the only casualties being everyone trying to be legitimate and want to financially support you, while the pirates continue to be pirates without a care in the world, as they WILL work around whatever system you try to have put into place.
Instead, make what you're putting up for sale worth it for people who  WILL give you money. Maybe people pirate because what you put up is overpriced for what it is? Maybe there's some element that would be better off spun off because people only want one part but don't want to pay for the entire package?
There will always be people who will never pay for anything, ruining the experience for everyone else to try in futility to stop those people is a exercise in frustration, for all parties involved that aren't the pirates.

@{6245df8fb4bad813bf989eb1|full_name}: I can understand how you feel! DMCA do take time but the report system for it doesn't exist. Like all you can report an avatar for is under "nudity"! 
And yeah, realitically it does take time to process and I respect that, but I don't see why we shouldn't request a more effecient way to quickly DMCA a ripped/ leaked model!
 Having more volunteers to help staff vrchat would be wonderful too! And I get it'll take a lot of effort and time, but I'm sure it'll be worth it, even for just the experience! 
Like investment. You put money in but the results will be there! But thank you for sharing your view points!
 I advocate for the opposite but I do enjoy reading everyone's ideas and different responses and solutions!!

@{6225212448fa527a93f3e67e|full_name}: What's being suggested here is the equivalent of using a molotov cocktail to solve a cockroach infestation in your house. Sure, the cockroaches are probably gone but so is about 90% of your house when all things are said and done.
As I mentioned before, Piracy is a service issue in most cases and isn't really something you can prevent through extreme measures like this. It would end up hurting legitimate creators more through abuse in comparison to any piracy it would solve through potentially taking down a world giving away stolen avatars.
The best thing you can do to curtail piracy and people stealing stuff is taking care of your paying customer base and make quality enough work that people look at you and say "Whoa, I wanna support this cool person and their work."
You can't stop someone deadset on pirating your content but you can do a lot to convert soft-piracy people into paying customers through less destructive means.
A potential idea that VRChat could do with this kind of mindset would be some kind of market system where verified content creators would have simpler means to point people in the direction of their respective shops. There's a lot of ways to approach this issue that doesn't involve handing a metaphorical gun to anyone who can fake a DMCA letter.

@{5f2f41c006be3a5585d43de0|full_name}: That's a very valid point! I do whole heartidly agree with how piracy can function the same way how avatars are and that it's basically impossible to retain everyone from leaking and ripping!
However, I feel like you don't need to hire millions considering that vrchat has 30k players and even less submit DMCA (cause half of them don't make avatars or publish them!)
Maybe like 50-100? To review each case and a lot of them are repeat offenders (making 20 public avatars under one author)! 
As for the avatar artist themselves! I can see how discounting them can prevent rippers, but rippers rip anything! Even free avatars sadly.  
Idk, I feel like avatars are valid enough to have a stronger protection from this platform! I don't see what's wrong trying something new and going back if it fails!
But I do respect your opinions and reality check! Some things are less feesible and difficult to impliment! But I do want to see a future where rippers/leakers get the punishment they deserve!

@{6225212448fa527a93f3e67e|full_name}: The first and most powerful way is the actual DMCA process. https://www.dmca.com/FAQ/How-can-I-file-a-DMCA-Takedown-Notice. Of course a more direct route is actually via copyright@vrchat.com or the legal address mentioned in the vrc copyright legal disclaimer regarding DMCA. Third the nudity should be only used if its a nudity avatar distributed with the public flag. The reporting system used to be more open to many specific things then got ground down to mostly useless system (external appearance observation). I do believe that there could be middle ground by generating a proper complaint ticketing system but you will still be dealing with delay because they will get flooded and there is a lot that goes into a proper DMCA review that is tedious. The best route is option 2 by addressing it as outlined by VRChat themselves.
Also: Mochi stay adorable, love your work.

@{62bb3c3a70a5022221383cec|full_name}: Oooo very valid point! I agree that you can not stop rippers completely! And it's very unfeesable to get rid of 100% of the problem... and I can see the unethical point of trolls abusing the report button!
However, the system we are implementing is hopefully "innocent until proven guilty", so even if trolls try to spam report you, you will be fine as long as you can prove the avatar has a purchased license! 
But I don't see an issue with trying to stop piracy! You agree that piracy is bad right? So why not give it a try to prevent it. Punishment is a good way to prevent and protect work! 
Yeah we can ask avatar creators to make their work cheaper, but I don't see why they need to change their marketing for the benefit of rippers/ leakers. Like, rippers still rip personal avatars sadly and I've seen them do it to free ones fjdnfnd!!
And a lot of companies sue conterfeit products using their trademark! It does help stigmitize the normalization of piracy and leaking!
But thank you for sharing! I do agree with your points as well as disagree! But respect it nevertheless!

@{6245df8fb4bad813bf989eb1|full_name}: omg yeah!! Maybe a middle ground! I totally would love that! A way for vrchat to not stress over DMCA system and for creators to have their work protected!
A direct process would work perfectly, vrchat will take a while to process if they are the third party between two opponents! 
A new reporting system will be perfect! So instead of us trying to spam "nudity" on a public avatar only for it to be re uploaded! A ticket would be nice to give the staff a better understanding of the situation! A lot of the report system is just a check mark box with limited options!
Awesome talking to you homie qwq! Ily and ty for being so understanding! I feel like debates should be tackling problems not each other! And solutions are to take in others' perspective instead of solidying our own ideologies with irrationality! But that's a debate for another day XD!

@{6225212448fa527a93f3e67e|full_name}: The entire point of what I stated was that you cannot prevent piracy in any meaningful capacity. Any solution people come up with tends to hurt paying customers more than the actual pirates, who will just find a way around it.
Plus I want to point out that what's being suggested is the exact opposite of an "Innocent til proven guilty" system. You keep throwing around that statement yet DMCA works in the exact opposite fashion of that since it acts on the presumption of guilt (DMCA is filed, offending item gets taken down until an internal investigation is completed or the accused manages to prove innocence, usually in court)

@{62bb3c3a70a5022221383cec|full_name}: I stated that it is impossible and unfeesable to remove piracy completely previously but can reduce it. And how would this hurt the customers? It's not as if we are going to get charged extra or penalized since we have the valid license to prove our innocence!
And if they investigate, our accounts will be fine because as long as they apply the rule of not holding our avatars until proven otherwise, there's literlly no reason to worry! Every avatar purchase has a verified license and we can just submit it. 
I don't see why avatar creators can't get their work supported? It doesn't harm anyone (except leakers and rippers) to add extra protection.
I feel like there's no reason to debate against supporting creator's work. It's just moral obligations to help them prevent their product from getting leaked constantly.
Furthermore, I think there's a miconception with your assumption of DMCA for vrchat. Twitter and youtube's terms of service with DMCA is to take down or demonetize a video if they are accused of copyright. 
However, the system we are trying to add into vrchat is to attempt to reduce leakers/ rippers via consequences (such as bans and perhaps legal lawsuits).
I have to repeat the innocent until proven guilty because it seems a little difficult to comprehend (understandably) and I have to emphasize due to misconception. 
There will be no consequences until proven guilty! 
Which means that vrchat will not file DMCA until! The avatar is proven ripped or leaked.
This should exist because some of my friends have had their avatars ripped and they work on it for a month it took them such a long time to work on and this would help them

I have had my work stolen and uploaded into a world that is fairly popular. After submitting a DMCA ticket I received no information on if my rights are being respected or if its even being looked into. This is very frustrating as an artist as this person is using my work to promote their own community twitch and patreon, and it seems like there is nothing I can do about it.

This is what I see happening:
* Try to start drama with individuals/communities you dont like.
* Claiming to send the DMCA on someones behalf and that not be the case
* Trolling the system to get a reaction out of someone (meaning there is no grounds for takedown. someone files it just to file it)
* Filing a claim and demanding money from the person reported to retract the claim (aka holding someones account as ransom)
This is a terrible idea, very easy to abuse.

@{6015a8dedd548068697b6112|full_name} To be fair, it requires the DMCA request to be legitimate, which includes the DMCA submitter to functionally doxx themselves. There might be a way to check if a DMCA request is at least valid in the first place.

details: This is common practice on other websites. After a DMCA is issued, the file is immediately taken down FOLLOWED BY an investigation into whether or not the file is copyright infringement. This means that it doesn't take days or even weeks for creators to get their intellectual property taken away from the game. Gets us one step closer to the 'creator protection' thet VRChat claims it's working towards.
title: When a public avatar is DMCA'd, immediately take the file down and THEN investigate
